question: Explain why the drift velocity of electrons in a conductor is very small, although electric current is established almost instantly when a potential difference is applied.

options.A: Current is established instantly because electrons move from one end of the wire to the other at the speed of light, so their drift speed is very high.
options.B: Drift velocity is zero after a potential difference is applied, but current arises due to stationary ions.
options.C: The field takes a long time to reach the electrons, so current is delayed even though drift speed is large.
options.D: The electric field is established throughout the conductor almost instantly, making electrons begin drifting nearly together; frequent collisions with ions keep their average drift velocity very small.
